title: When Should You Actually Buy Individual Stocks?
meta_title: When to Buy Individual Stocks: My 6 Conditions
subtitle: Your SIP is boring, a friend's stock just tripled, and the itch to pick your own winners is real. I have bought single stocks and still hold a few, but I am moving that money into index funds. Here are the six conditions that all have to be true before I buy a company.
description: The honest rules for buying individual stocks instead of just an index fund. Six conditions, only while accumulating, foundation secured, under 5% of the portfolio, value over hype, a long horizon, and inside your circle of competence, plus why any risky bet has to be your own thesis and how a small slice diverted from the index can cost 7 to 11 crore in lost compounding.
toast: I run six conditions before I buy a single stock, and if even one is missing, I leave it alone. That rule has saved me more money than any pick ever made me.
That 30 to 50 lakh you play with in stocks is really 7 to 11 crore of future money once it compounds. Every rupee that fails to beat the index is quietly costing you a fortune.

faqs.question: Should I buy individual stocks or index funds?
faqs.answer: For the large majority of your money, index funds. Individual stocks make sense only as a small slice of around 3% to 5% of your portfolio, and only when you are still earning, your financial foundation is secure, you are buying businesses you actually understand, and the decision is your own thesis rather than a tip. Even then, expect the index to quietly outperform your picks over time.

faqs.question: How much of my portfolio should be in individual stocks?
faqs.answer: Keep every individual stock combined to about 3% to 5% of your total portfolio, not 3% to 5% per stock. A useful way to size it is against your withdrawal rate. If you plan to withdraw at most 4% a year, that 4% is one year of your spending, so a slice of about that size going to zero costs you roughly one survivable year and your retirement date barely moves.

faqs.question: Is stock picking gambling?
faqs.answer: It becomes gambling the moment you buy something you do not understand, bet more than you can afford to lose, act on someone else's tip, or chase a stock purely because it is going up. It stays closer to investing when you buy businesses inside your own circle of competence, on your own thesis, at a price backed by real earnings, with a small position size and a long horizon.

faqs.question: Can I beat the market by picking my own stocks?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Most people, including professional fund managers, underperform a simple index fund over a decade once you account for taxes and mistakes. Worse, the money you divert into picks that underperform loses decades of compounding, so a 30 to 50 lakh slice can quietly cost you 7 to 11 crore of future wealth. Pick because you enjoy it and understand the businesses, keep it small, and treat any outperformance as a bonus.
